result.rationale:
TopicEmbed#import builds the footer via string interpolation: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` with no escaping, and only guards with `url =~ /^https?\:///`. A URL like `http://x/' onmouseover='...` or containing `>` can break out of the attribute/anchor and inject arbitrary HTML, which is stored as post content (cook_method raw_html) and rendered. The finding's mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the footer HTML is built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. A crafted URL like `http://x.com' onclick='alert(1)` still matches and would break out of the single-quoted href attribute and inject arbitrary markup/JS into `contents`. Because the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, the injected HTML is not escaped/sanitized and will be rendered (`raw post.cooked` in embed view).
